record.original_question: (Epstein) Let M be a PL manifold. Is PL0 (M ), the group of PL homeomorphisms of M that are isotopic to the identity, a simple group?

evidence.quote: Question 9.5. (Epstein) Let M be a PL manifold. Is PL0 (M ), the group of PL homeomorphisms of M that are isotopic to the identity, a simple group?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $M$ be a piecewise-linear (PL) manifold (possibly with boundary), and let $\mathrm{PL}(M)$ denote the group of PL homeomorphisms of $M$ (with compact support if $M$ is non-compact). Define $\mathrm{PL}_0(M) \subseteq \mathrm{PL}(M)$ to be the subgroup consisting of those PL homeomorphisms that are PL-isotopic to the identity through a compactly supported PL isotopy. Determine whether $\mathrm{PL}_0(M)$ is a simple group; that is, decide whether it has no nontrivial proper normal subgroups.
artifact.status_search_result: The simplicity of identity components of PL homeomorphism groups (Epstein's question) is generally regarded as an open problem. While the analogous results are known for $C^r$-diffeomorphism groups (Epstein–Herman–Mather–Thurston) and for groups of homeomorphisms isotopic to the identity, the PL case for general PL manifolds remains unresolved in the literature, with no general proof or counterexample available.

status_evidence.title: The simplicity of certain groups of homeomorphisms (Epstein)
status_evidence.snippet: Epstein's general criterion gives sufficient conditions for the commutator subgroup of a group of homeomorphisms to be simple; the PL case requires perfectness which is not established for all PL manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: Epstein's framework reduces simplicity of PL_0(M) to perfectness of the group, which is not generally known.

status_evidence.title: PL(M) admits no Polish group topology (K. Mann)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies algebraic and topological structure of PL(M) for PL manifolds; references open questions regarding normal subgroup structure of identity components.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature treats simplicity of PL_0(M) as a structural question still under investigation.
